info.title: Vercel KV
info.description:
The Vercel KV data plane, which is Upstash Redis behind a Vercel host.

THIS DOCUMENT IS AUTHORED, NOT VENDORED. Every other document under specs/ is the vendor's own bytes, pinned by the sha256 in specs/mirror.lock so that an unannounced upstream change lands as a reviewable diff. There is nothing to pin here: neither Vercel nor Upstash publishes a machine-readable description of this surface. Upstash publishes three OpenAPI documents -- QStash, Workflow, and a Developer API that is the management plane at api.upstash.com/v2 (create a database, change a plan) -- and none of them describes the command endpoint. Vercel's own document describes blob-store management and no KV commands at all. Both vendors document the data plane in prose.

So the lock records this file with source `authored`, and its hash still pins the bytes: an edit to this document is a visible diff like any other. What is absent is the refetch, because there is no upstream to refetch from -- which means this document cannot tell you the vendor changed something. Treat every statement in it as `authored` provenance, the same grade the behavior bundle carries, and downgrade it the moment a probe or a published description contradicts it.

The surface transcribed here is the one the deleted Go pack served, which is the Upstash REST convention: POST / with the command as a JSON array, answering {result}. It is deliberately the narrow subset that pack implemented rather than the whole Redis command set, because the subset is what there is evidence for.

servers.description: Vercel KV data plane. Deployments address a per-store subdomain of this host.

post.description: The request body is the command and its arguments as a JSON array: ["SET", "key", "value"]. The response carries the reply under `result`, whose type follows the command -- a status string for SET, the stored value or null for GET, a count for DEL.

400.description: The command was absent, unknown, or missing arguments.

RedisCommand.description: The command name followed by its arguments. Upstash upper-cases the name on the way in, so ["get","k"] and ["GET","k"] are the same command.

result.description: The reply. A status string for SET, the stored value or null for a GET that missed, the number of keys removed for DEL.
